rows.label: first-order tissue consumption rate k (tirapazamine)
rows.quantity: the engine's first-order interstitial loss rate k (1/s) — the -kC sink of the transport PDE — vs the MEASURED anoxic metabolic consumption rate constant of tirapazamine fitted in the same position of the same diffusion-reaction equation
rows.predicted: TWO readings that differ by 7x and land on OPPOSITE sides of the measurement: k_raw = clearance + binding = 9.747e-05 /s (0.0112-0.0189x measured), and k_calibrated = clearance + alpha*binding = 6.918e-04 /s at alpha = 22.2235 (0.080-0.134x measured)
rows.note: WHAT MAY HONESTLY BE SAID, AND IT IS NOW WEAKER THAN IT WAS. Before the two-route promotion the magnitude alpha implied for a small-molecule interstitial loss rate landed within 2x of one independently measured rate constant of the same class, in a fit that saw no tirapazamine, no MCL and no rate constant — weaker than validation, stronger than nothing (results/external_anchor_survey.md sec. 3.3). At the new alpha it lands 7.5-12.5x below that measurement instead. THIS IS THE COST SIDE OF THE PROMOTION AND IT IS NOT COSMETIC: the same change that brought the dimensionless hindrance row inside its band pushed this reading out of its own. The two anchors are coupled — the Primeau penetration fit pins the RATIO D/k, so lowering D lowers k by the same factor — and they now disagree about where the engine sits. That disagreement is unresolved and is the sharpest open question the promotion leaves (results/two_route_promotion.md sec. 8).
rows.reason: PARTIALLY COMMENSURABLE ONLY, and the owning survey says so before any number is quoted. TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS, either sufficient. (1) THE PROCESS IS NOT THE SAME PROCESS. The measured constant is ANOXIC BIOREDUCTIVE METABOLISM of a hypoxia-activated prodrug — a real, drug-specific consumption reaction that the engine's panel drugs do not have — while the engine's k is a generic binding-plus-clearance sink. Same units, same slot in the same equation, DIFFERENT PHYSICAL PROCESS. results/external_anchor_survey.md sec. 2.1 declares it a measured ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE BOUND on how large a real interstitial consumption rate can be, and explicitly NOT a like-for-like score. (2) THE ENGINE HAS NO SINGLE NUMBER TO SCORE. k_raw and k_calibrated differ by 7x and straddle the measurement: the uncalibrated sink is 53-89x TOO SMALL (which independently reproduces results/pk_reality.md's ~300x diagnosis on a different drug, in a different system, against a directly measured rate constant rather than a penetration depth — that FAIL-shaped fact is recorded here, not suppressed), while the alpha-amplified sink lands within 1.2-2.0x. Picking the flattering reading would manufacture a PASS and picking the other would manufacture a FAIL, and nothing about this anchor determines the choice. NOTE WHICH WAY THIS COSTS — AND THAT IT REVERSED. Until results/two_route_promotion.md, scoring this row on k_calibrated would have PASSED the repo's 3x band (0.49-0.82x measured at alpha = 148.6082), so declining to score removed a PASS from the tally. The promotion cut alpha to 22.2235 — because doxorubicin's compiled D fell 6.6x and alpha is fitted from L = sqrt(D/k) against the same measured anchor — and k_calibrated fell with it. Scored on k_calibrated TODAY this row would FAIL: 0.080-0.134x measured, i.e. 7.5-12.5x TOO SMALL, outside the 3x band. So declining to score now removes a FAILURE from the tally, not a pass. The decision not to score is unchanged and rests on reason (1), which is about commensurability and is untouched by any of this; what changed is which way the omission flatters us, and that is stated here rather than left as a stale claim.

rows.note: Not a null result: the DISCRIMINATING version of this same comparison is the breast row below, which the engine FAILS by ~40x. Read the two together. The screened-Poisson screening length sqrt(K/(a+d)) has median 7.1 um (GBM) and 6.2 um (breast), BELOW the 12 um production spacing at 99.78% and 99.92% of tissue nodes respectively.
rows.reason: THE ANCHOR CANNOT DISCRIMINATE, for three independent reasons, and the engine's number would sit inside it either way. (1) UNCERTAINTY. The paper's Statistical analysis section states verbatim that 'the data are presented as the mean +/- standard deviation', so 2.5 is an SD over 11 patients, not an SEM. On a non-negative quantity that the solver clips at zero, mean +/- 1 SD is effectively 0.0-4.5 mmHg, and the paper's own per-patient table has 10 of 11 tumours in 0.0-3.0 INCLUDING A MEASURED 0.0. Any engine output from nothing up to 4.5 mmHg passes. A verdict that cannot be failed is not a verdict. (2) IT DOES NOT SEPARATE TUMOUR FROM NORMAL TISSUE. Less 1992 (PMID 1423283) measured normal human tissue at 2 +/- 4 mmHg, n=11, by the SAME wick-in-needle technique with Boucher and Jain on both author lists. The intracranial-tumour figure is statistically indistinguishable from it, so agreement with it is not evidence that the engine reproduces tumour interstitial hypertension -- it is equally consistent with the engine having no tumour effect at all, which on this section is close to what it has. (3) TREATED, DECOMPRESSED STATE. All 11 patients received dexamethasone 10 mg + mannitol 0.5 mg/kg + furosemide 20 mg i.v. and were hyperventilated to PaCO2 25-32 mmHg, and IFP was taken after the cranium was opened and the dura removed. The authors' own conclusion is that 'antioedema therapy in patients with brain tumours is responsible in part for the low tumour IFP', and the same paper measures a 17-50% fall in rodent tumour IFP from hypocapnia alone (27 +/- 15 -> 18 +/- 10 mmHg). The engine models no steroid, no osmotic agent, no diuretic and no decompression, so even a matching number would be matching a different physiological state. COMMENSURABILITY. A wick-in-needle probe is a 23-gauge needle whose side hole equilibrates with the mobile interstitial fluid over a sub-millimetre to millimetre contact region, at ONE placement inside the tumour mass. The commensurable model statistic is therefore the solved field's local mean over a wick-sized window at tumour-bearing locations -- NOT the domain mean, NOT the field maximum, and NOT the landing page's iso-contour levels, which are fractions of a coarse-grained maximum chosen for rendering. Reported here as the median over placements at a 250 um Gaussian window over nodes with tumour occupancy >= 0.5; the 125 um and 500 um windows are in results/sweep/ifp_validation.json and move it by under 1.4x.

rows.label: IFP solve is under-resolved on every grid the engine runs at
rows.quantity: screened-Poisson screening length sqrt(K/(a+d)) implied by physics/pressure.py's own shipped coefficients vs the grid spacings the engine actually solves on (8-30 um)
rows.predicted: median screening length 7.1 um (GBM) / 6.2 um (breast); L/dx = 0.59 / 0.51 at the 12 um production spacing
rows.measured: n/a — this row is scored against the discretisation, not against a measurement
rows.note: Grid ladder, wick-scale tumour median: GBM 0.358 -> 0.434 -> 0.462 -> 0.370 mmHg and breast 0.621 -> 0.424 -> 0.370 -> 0.286 mmHg at dx = 24, 18, 12, 8 um. Full ladder in results/sweep/ifp_validation.json.
rows.reason: NO MEASUREMENT IS INVOLVED; this row is registered so that the two rows above cannot be quoted without it. The screened-Poisson screening length sqrt(K/(a+d)) has median 7.1 um (GBM) and 6.2 um (breast), BELOW the 12 um production spacing at 99.78% and 99.92% of tissue nodes respectively. A screened-Poisson solve whose screening length is below the mesh cannot represent the operator it discretises: the reaction term dominates the diagonal (median (a+d)*dx^2/K = 2.9 on GBM, 3.8 on breast), so each node relaxes toward its own LOCAL algebraic equilibrium a*p_v/(a+d) with the Laplacian barely coupling neighbours. Measured directly: the solved field correlates with that pointwise algebraic limit at r = 0.92 (GBM) and 0.94 (breast). At production dx the 'solved pressure field' is therefore closer to a pointwise nonlinear map of the vascular-density KDE than to a transport solve, and the margin pressure gradient that carries the Jain effect into the convection term is not resolved. Refining the mesh does not fix it and is not free: the field is not grid-converged either (see the ifp-grid-unconverged conditional), and pressure.py's tumour-occupancy smoothing _TUMOR_SIGMA = 5.0 is specified in GRID CELLS, so the physical smoothing scale is itself a function of dx (60 um at dx=12, 120 um at dx=24) and the model changes as the mesh changes.

conditionals.alpha-fit: Inherits alpha, the single free constant fit ONCE in closed form to the doxorubicin perivascular anchor (PMID 16361566) by validation.calibration.calibrate_alpha. Anything downstream of alpha is conditional on that one fit and is not independent of it.
conditionals.analytic-only: Computed in closed form from molecular descriptors; the transport PDE is never invoked. Verified by call-counter instrumentation in results/transvascular_exchange_revalidation.md sec. 6.1. This row cannot confirm or refute the solver.
conditionals.band-wider-than-assay: The literature band is wider than the assay spread it is meant to correct (the 2-D reference's own IQR is ~19x, PMID 34794398), so a pass here is a weak pass by construction (results/kill_calibration.md).
conditionals.cell-exclusion-default-off: The cellular volume-exclusion term (molecular/ecm_mesh.py::cell_exclusion, Maxwell's impermeable-inclusion limit) is MERGED BUT NOT WIRED IN. results/cellular_exclusion.md sec. 7 recommends merging the physics and explicitly NOT flipping the default; nothing in compile_drug calls it, so DrugParams.diffusivity is bit-identical to the pre-merge value. Every VERDICT in this group is therefore scored on the engine AS IT SHIPS, with the term OFF. The cell-term-ON arm is reported alongside each verdict and carries three caveats of its own, none of which is a footnote: (a) phi_cell = 0.7892 is measured by Delesse's principle on the repo's real Xenium BREAST TUMOUR section and then applied to a V79 hamster multicellular layer — a literature search for an MCL extracellular-volume measurement returned nothing usable, so the packing density is imported from the wrong system (cellular_exclusion.md sec. 4.1); (b) Xenium's boundary segmentation tiles the section, so phi_cell is an UPPER estimate and every hindrance derived from it is too; (c) stacking the cell term on the existing chain DOUBLE-COUNTS by up to ~1.9x, because brownian.py's 300 nm obstacle field and ALPHA_TORTUOSITY = 0.6 were partly standing in for cell-scale obstruction, and cellular_exclusion.md sec. 5.3 states in terms that it cannot resolve which.
conditionals.coefficient-not-field: This row scores an INPUT COEFFICIENT of the transport PDE, not any solved field. The prediction is read straight off MolecularProfile after descriptors.from_smiles -> compile_drug.build_profile; the solver is never entered, verified by a call counter on physics.diffusion.simulate_drug_transport and sim.engine.simulate_response and recorded in results/anchor_registration.md sec. 3. It is a stronger row than an unanchored coefficient and a weaker one than a field test: it can FALSIFY the hindrance law, and it cannot confirm or refute the solver.
conditionals.gdsc-potency: Intrinsic potency comes from the GDSC cell-line screen, not from this patient's tissue; the 3-D:2-D ratio therefore constrains the PRODUCT of delivery and cell-state resistance, not either factor alone (results/kill_calibration.md).
conditionals.ifp-grid-unconverged: The wick-scale IFP statistic is not grid-converged. Across dx = 24, 18, 12, 8 um it moves 0.358 -> 0.434 -> 0.462 -> 0.370 mmHg on GBM (non-monotone, 1.29x spread) and 0.621 -> 0.424 -> 0.370 -> 0.286 mmHg on breast (monotone, 2.17x spread, still falling 22.5% over the last refinement with no plateau). Two contributions are known: the vascular-density KDE is rebuilt per grid, and _TUMOR_SIGMA = 5.0 in pressure.py is specified in GRID CELLS, so the physical tumour smoothing scale is 40/60/90/120 um at dx = 8/12/18/24 um and the model itself changes with the mesh.
conditionals.ifp-uncalibrated: Every coefficient in tmesim/physics/pressure.py is a hardcoded order-of-magnitude constant, by its own docstring 'not patient-calibrated': _K0 = 1.2, _K_ECM_ATTEN = 0.6, _PV = 25.0 mmHg, _LP_NORMAL = 1e-3, _LEAK_GAIN = 12.0, _LAMBDA_LYMPH = 3e-2. None was fitted to any measurement, which makes any IFP score genuinely out-of-sample — and also means nothing constrains the absolute scale. _PV = 25.0 in particular is an upper bound on the predicted core plateau and was NOT chosen against any of the anchors scored here.
conditionals.ifp-unresolved-mesh: The screened-Poisson screening length sqrt(K/(a+d)) implied by those coefficients is ~6-7 um on both real sections, BELOW every grid spacing the engine runs at (8-30 um), at >99.7% of tissue nodes. The reaction term dominates the diagonal, so the discrete solution collapses toward the pointwise algebraic limit a*p_v/(a+d) (measured correlation r = 0.90 GBM / 0.93 breast) and the interior Laplacian barely couples neighbours. Any IFP number is conditional on a mesh that does not resolve the operator being solved (results/ifp_validation.md sec. 5).
conditionals.leak-fit: The additive paracellular leak constant reconstruct.barrier.L_PARACELLULAR_LEAK = 0.238 was FITTED to the same contrast-enhancing-vs-non-enhancing contrasts these rows are scored against, so the leak-on score is not fully out-of-sample (results/glioma_regional_pk.md).
conditionals.mcl-no-vasculature: COMMENSURABILITY BOUND, and it is the load-bearing caveat on this group. A multicellular layer is a stack of cells grown on a porous support: packed cells, little stroma, NO VASCULATURE, no necrosis, no interstitial convection and no plasma source term. Hicks measured flux across that slab and fitted it to a diffusion-reaction equation of the SAME FORM the engine solves, which is exactly what makes D and k commensurable AS COEFFICIENTS. What that licenses: scoring the engine's compiled per-drug D_eff, and the hindrance law that produces it, against a directly measured tissue diffusion coefficient in the same units and the same functional role. What it does NOT license: any claim about a vascularised tissue section. Nothing in an MCL constrains vessel spacing, the transvascular source term, IFP-driven convection, or the spatial concentration field the solver produces on real reconstructed geometry. Reading an MCL row as evidence that the engine's tissue predictions are validated would be the modality pooling results/external_anchor_survey.md sec. 0 catalogues three live instances of, and which this project has manufactured a false regression from twice.
conditionals.ps-scale: Conditional on an UNCALIBRATED unit scale. tmesim/treatment/drugs.py::PS_SCALE_S_INV = 1.0 is an implicit, undocumented, underived conversion from a dimensionless product to a rate in 1/s; nothing in the repo derives it. See results/transvascular_exchange_revalidation.md sec. 6.2. Every transvascular-exchange-ON number carries this.
conditionals.untreated-section: The open spatial section is an UNTREATED resection. There is no paired measured drug response on this tissue; the anchor is a cohort-level literature value, not this patient's outcome.

rows.label: first-order tissue consumption rate k (tirapazamine)
rows.quantity: the engine's first-order interstitial loss rate k (1/s) — the -kC sink of the transport PDE — vs the MEASURED anoxic metabolic consumption rate constant of tirapazamine fitted in the same position of the same diffusion-reaction equation
rows.predicted: TWO readings that differ by 6x and land on OPPOSITE sides of the measurement: k_raw = clearance + binding = 1.048e-04 /s (0.0121-0.0203x measured), and k_calibrated = clearance + alpha*binding = 6.033e-04 /s at alpha = 15.1009 (0.070-0.117x measured)
rows.note: WHAT MAY HONESTLY BE SAID, AND IT IS NOW WEAKER THAN IT WAS. Before the two-route promotion the magnitude alpha implied for a small-molecule interstitial loss rate landed within 2x of one independently measured rate constant of the same class, in a fit that saw no tirapazamine, no MCL and no rate constant — weaker than validation, stronger than nothing (results/external_anchor_survey.md sec. 3.3). At the new alpha it lands 8.6-14.4x below that measurement instead. THIS IS THE COST SIDE OF THE PROMOTION AND IT IS NOT COSMETIC: the same change that brought the dimensionless hindrance row inside its band pushed this reading out of its own. The two anchors are coupled — the Primeau penetration fit pins the RATIO D/k, so lowering D lowers k by the same factor — and they now disagree about where the engine sits. That disagreement is unresolved and is the sharpest open question the promotion leaves (results/two_route_promotion.md sec. 8).
rows.reason: PARTIALLY COMMENSURABLE ONLY, and the owning survey says so before any number is quoted. TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS, either sufficient. (1) THE PROCESS IS NOT THE SAME PROCESS. The measured constant is ANOXIC BIOREDUCTIVE METABOLISM of a hypoxia-activated prodrug — a real, drug-specific consumption reaction that the engine's panel drugs do not have — while the engine's k is a generic binding-plus-clearance sink. Same units, same slot in the same equation, DIFFERENT PHYSICAL PROCESS. results/external_anchor_survey.md sec. 2.1 declares it a measured ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE BOUND on how large a real interstitial consumption rate can be, and explicitly NOT a like-for-like score. (2) THE ENGINE HAS NO SINGLE NUMBER TO SCORE. k_raw and k_calibrated differ by 6x and straddle the measurement: the uncalibrated sink is 53-89x TOO SMALL (which independently reproduces results/pk_reality.md's ~300x diagnosis on a different drug, in a different system, against a directly measured rate constant rather than a penetration depth — that FAIL-shaped fact is recorded here, not suppressed), while the alpha-amplified sink lands within 1.2-2.0x. Picking the flattering reading would manufacture a PASS and picking the other would manufacture a FAIL, and nothing about this anchor determines the choice. NOTE WHICH WAY THIS COSTS — AND THAT IT REVERSED. Until results/two_route_promotion.md, scoring this row on k_calibrated would have PASSED the repo's 3x band (0.49-0.82x measured at alpha = 148.6082), so declining to score removed a PASS from the tally. The promotion cut alpha to 22.2235 — because doxorubicin's compiled D fell 6.6x and alpha is fitted from L = sqrt(D/k) against the same measured anchor — and k_calibrated fell with it. Scored on k_calibrated TODAY this row would FAIL: 0.070-0.117x measured, i.e. 8.6-14.4x TOO SMALL, outside the 3x band. So declining to score now removes a FAILURE from the tally, not a pass. The decision not to score is unchanged and rests on reason (1), which is about commensurability and is untouched by any of this; what changed is which way the omission flatters us, and that is stated here rather than left as a stale claim.

rows.label: GBM section IFP vs human intracranial-tumour IFP
rows.quantity: solved interstitial fluid pressure (mmHg) at wick-scale placements in the tumour mass of the real Xenium GBM section vs MEASURED intraoperative wick-in-needle IFP in human intracranial tumours
rows.measured: 2.0 +/- 2.5 mmHg (mean +/- SD, n=11); 10 of 11 tumours lay in 0.0-3.0, one astrocytoma at 9.5; glioblastoma-only subset n=5 mean 1.2, range 0.0-3.0

rows.note: Not a null result: the DISCRIMINATING version of this same comparison is the breast row below, which the engine FAILS by ~40x. Read the two together. The screened-Poisson screening length sqrt(K/(a+d)) has median 7.1 um (GBM) and 6.2 um (breast), BELOW the 12 um production spacing at 99.78% and 99.92% of tissue nodes respectively.
rows.reason: THE ANCHOR CANNOT DISCRIMINATE, for three independent reasons, and the engine's number would sit inside it either way. (1) UNCERTAINTY. The paper's Statistical analysis section states verbatim that 'the data are presented as the mean +/- standard deviation', so 2.5 is an SD over 11 patients, not an SEM. On a non-negative quantity that the solver clips at zero, mean +/- 1 SD is effectively 0.0-4.5 mmHg, and the paper's own per-patient table has 10 of 11 tumours in 0.0-3.0 INCLUDING A MEASURED 0.0. Any engine output from nothing up to 4.5 mmHg passes. A verdict that cannot be failed is not a verdict. (2) IT DOES NOT SEPARATE TUMOUR FROM NORMAL TISSUE. Less 1992 (PMID 1423283) measured normal human tissue at 2 +/- 4 mmHg, n=11, by the SAME wick-in-needle technique with Boucher and Jain on both author lists. The intracranial-tumour figure is statistically indistinguishable from it, so agreement with it is not evidence that the engine reproduces tumour interstitial hypertension -- it is equally consistent with the engine having no tumour effect at all, which on this section is close to what it has. (3) TREATED, DECOMPRESSED STATE. All 11 patients received dexamethasone 10 mg + mannitol 0.5 mg/kg + furosemide 20 mg i.v. and were hyperventilated to PaCO2 25-32 mmHg, and IFP was taken after the cranium was opened and the dura removed. The authors' own conclusion is that 'antioedema therapy in patients with brain tumours is responsible in part for the low tumour IFP', and the same paper measures a 17-50% fall in rodent tumour IFP from hypocapnia alone (27 +/- 15 -> 18 +/- 10 mmHg). The engine models no steroid, no osmotic agent, no diuretic and no decompression, so even a matching number would be matching a different physiological state. COMMENSURABILITY. A wick-in-needle probe is a 23-gauge needle whose side hole equilibrates with the mobile interstitial fluid over a sub-millimetre to millimetre contact region, at ONE placement inside the tumour mass. The commensurable model statistic is therefore the solved field's local mean over a wick-sized window at tumour-bearing locations -- NOT the domain mean, NOT the field maximum, and NOT the landing page's iso-contour levels, which are fractions of a coarse-grained maximum chosen for rendering. Reported here as the median over placements at a 250 um Gaussian window over nodes with tumour occupancy >= 0.5; the 125 um and 500 um windows are in results/sweep/ifp_validation.json and move it by under 1.4x.

rows.label: IFP solve is under-resolved on every grid the engine runs at
rows.quantity: screened-Poisson screening length sqrt(K/(a+d)) implied by physics/pressure.py's own shipped coefficients vs the grid spacings the engine actually solves on (8-30 um)
rows.predicted: median screening length 7.1 um (GBM) / 6.2 um (breast); L/dx = 0.59 / 0.51 at the 12 um production spacing
rows.measured: n/a — this row is scored against the discretisation, not against a measurement
rows.note: Grid ladder, wick-scale tumour median: GBM 0.358 -> 0.434 -> 0.462 -> 0.370 mmHg and breast 0.621 -> 0.424 -> 0.370 -> 0.286 mmHg at dx = 24, 18, 12, 8 um. Full ladder in results/sweep/ifp_validation.json.
rows.reason: NO MEASUREMENT IS INVOLVED; this row is registered so that the two rows above cannot be quoted without it. The screened-Poisson screening length sqrt(K/(a+d)) has median 7.1 um (GBM) and 6.2 um (breast), BELOW the 12 um production spacing at 99.78% and 99.92% of tissue nodes respectively. A screened-Poisson solve whose screening length is below the mesh cannot represent the operator it discretises: the reaction term dominates the diagonal (median (a+d)*dx^2/K = 2.9 on GBM, 3.8 on breast), so each node relaxes toward its own LOCAL algebraic equilibrium a*p_v/(a+d) with the Laplacian barely coupling neighbours. Measured directly: the solved field correlates with that pointwise algebraic limit at r = 0.92 (GBM) and 0.94 (breast). At production dx the 'solved pressure field' is therefore closer to a pointwise nonlinear map of the vascular-density KDE than to a transport solve, and the margin pressure gradient that carries the Jain effect into the convection term is not resolved. Refining the mesh does not fix it and is not free: the field is not grid-converged either (see the ifp-grid-unconverged conditional), and pressure.py's tumour-occupancy smoothing _TUMOR_SIGMA = 5.0 is specified in GRID CELLS, so the physical smoothing scale is itself a function of dx (60 um at dx=12, 120 um at dx=24) and the model changes as the mesh changes.

conditionals.alpha-fit: Inherits alpha, the single free constant fit ONCE in closed form to the doxorubicin perivascular anchor (PMID 16361566) by validation.calibration.calibrate_alpha. Anything downstream of alpha is conditional on that one fit and is not independent of it.
conditionals.analytic-only: Computed in closed form from molecular descriptors; the transport PDE is never invoked. Verified by call-counter instrumentation in results/transvascular_exchange_revalidation.md sec. 6.1. This row cannot confirm or refute the solver.
conditionals.band-wider-than-assay: The literature band is wider than the assay spread it is meant to correct (the 2-D reference's own IQR is ~19x, PMID 34794398), so a pass here is a weak pass by construction (results/kill_calibration.md).
conditionals.cell-exclusion-default-off: The cellular volume-exclusion term (molecular/ecm_mesh.py::cell_exclusion, Maxwell's impermeable-inclusion limit) is MERGED BUT NOT WIRED IN. results/cellular_exclusion.md sec. 7 recommends merging the physics and explicitly NOT flipping the default; nothing in compile_drug calls it, so DrugParams.diffusivity is bit-identical to the pre-merge value. Every VERDICT in this group is therefore scored on the engine AS IT SHIPS, with the term OFF. The cell-term-ON arm is reported alongside each verdict and carries three caveats of its own, none of which is a footnote: (a) phi_cell = 0.7892 is measured by Delesse's principle on the repo's real Xenium BREAST TUMOUR section and then applied to a V79 hamster multicellular layer — a literature search for an MCL extracellular-volume measurement returned nothing usable, so the packing density is imported from the wrong system (cellular_exclusion.md sec. 4.1); (b) Xenium's boundary segmentation tiles the section, so phi_cell is an UPPER estimate and every hindrance derived from it is too; (c) stacking the cell term on the existing chain DOUBLE-COUNTS by up to ~1.9x, because brownian.py's 300 nm obstacle field and ALPHA_TORTUOSITY = 0.6 were partly standing in for cell-scale obstruction, and cellular_exclusion.md sec. 5.3 states in terms that it cannot resolve which.
conditionals.coefficient-not-field: This row scores an INPUT COEFFICIENT of the transport PDE, not any solved field. The prediction is read straight off MolecularProfile after descriptors.from_smiles -> compile_drug.build_profile; the solver is never entered, verified by a call counter on physics.diffusion.simulate_drug_transport and sim.engine.simulate_response and recorded in results/anchor_registration.md sec. 3. It is a stronger row than an unanchored coefficient and a weaker one than a field test: it can FALSIFY the hindrance law, and it cannot confirm or refute the solver.
conditionals.gdsc-potency: Intrinsic potency comes from the GDSC cell-line screen, not from this patient's tissue; the 3-D:2-D ratio therefore constrains the PRODUCT of delivery and cell-state resistance, not either factor alone (results/kill_calibration.md).
conditionals.ifp-grid-unconverged: The wick-scale IFP statistic is not grid-converged. Across dx = 24, 18, 12, 8 um it moves 0.358 -> 0.434 -> 0.462 -> 0.370 mmHg on GBM (non-monotone, 1.29x spread) and 0.621 -> 0.424 -> 0.370 -> 0.286 mmHg on breast (monotone, 2.17x spread, still falling 22.5% over the last refinement with no plateau). Two contributions are known: the vascular-density KDE is rebuilt per grid, and _TUMOR_SIGMA = 5.0 in pressure.py is specified in GRID CELLS, so the physical tumour smoothing scale is 40/60/90/120 um at dx = 8/12/18/24 um and the model itself changes with the mesh.
conditionals.ifp-uncalibrated: Every coefficient in tmesim/physics/pressure.py is a hardcoded order-of-magnitude constant, by its own docstring 'not patient-calibrated': _K0 = 1.2, _K_ECM_ATTEN = 0.6, _PV = 25.0 mmHg, _LP_NORMAL = 1e-3, _LEAK_GAIN = 12.0, _LAMBDA_LYMPH = 3e-2. None was fitted to any measurement, which makes any IFP score genuinely out-of-sample — and also means nothing constrains the absolute scale. _PV = 25.0 in particular is an upper bound on the predicted core plateau and was NOT chosen against any of the anchors scored here.
conditionals.ifp-unresolved-mesh: The screened-Poisson screening length sqrt(K/(a+d)) implied by those coefficients is ~6-7 um on both real sections, BELOW every grid spacing the engine runs at (8-30 um), at >99.7% of tissue nodes. The reaction term dominates the diagonal, so the discrete solution collapses toward the pointwise algebraic limit a*p_v/(a+d) (measured correlation r = 0.90 GBM / 0.93 breast) and the interior Laplacian barely couples neighbours. Any IFP number is conditional on a mesh that does not resolve the operator being solved (results/ifp_validation.md sec. 5).
conditionals.leak-fit: The additive paracellular leak constant reconstruct.barrier.L_PARACELLULAR_LEAK = 0.238 was FITTED to the same contrast-enhancing-vs-non-enhancing contrasts these rows are scored against, so the leak-on score is not fully out-of-sample (results/glioma_regional_pk.md).
conditionals.mcl-no-vasculature: COMMENSURABILITY BOUND, and it is the load-bearing caveat on this group. A multicellular layer is a stack of cells grown on a porous support: packed cells, little stroma, NO VASCULATURE, no necrosis, no interstitial convection and no plasma source term. Hicks measured flux across that slab and fitted it to a diffusion-reaction equation of the SAME FORM the engine solves, which is exactly what makes D and k commensurable AS COEFFICIENTS. What that licenses: scoring the engine's compiled per-drug D_eff, and the hindrance law that produces it, against a directly measured tissue diffusion coefficient in the same units and the same functional role. What it does NOT license: any claim about a vascularised tissue section. Nothing in an MCL constrains vessel spacing, the transvascular source term, IFP-driven convection, or the spatial concentration field the solver produces on real reconstructed geometry. Reading an MCL row as evidence that the engine's tissue predictions are validated would be the modality pooling results/external_anchor_survey.md sec. 0 catalogues three live instances of, and which this project has manufactured a false regression from twice.
conditionals.ps-scale: Conditional on an UNCALIBRATED unit scale. tmesim/treatment/drugs.py::PS_SCALE_S_INV = 1.0 is an implicit, undocumented, underived conversion from a dimensionless product to a rate in 1/s; nothing in the repo derives it. See results/transvascular_exchange_revalidation.md sec. 6.2. Every transvascular-exchange-ON number carries this.
conditionals.untreated-section: The open spatial section is an UNTREATED resection. There is no paired measured drug response on this tissue; the anchor is a cohort-level literature value, not this patient's outcome.
